safety-information.danger: Never expose the camera to rain, moisture, or submersion in water. Doing so may cause electric shock or fire.
safety-information.warning: Keep memory cards, batteries, and small accessories away from children. Swallowing may cause serious injury.
safety-information.caution: Avoid pointing the lens directly at the sun or strong light sources. Permanent sensor damage may result.
safety-information.note: Always use the included wrist strap when shooting in environments where the camera could be dropped.

section.paragraph: Familiarize yourself with the physical controls and ports before operating the camera for the first time.

subsection.paragraph: The top panel houses the primary shooting controls designed for quick adjustment without removing the camera from your eye.
subsection.control: Selects the shooting mode. Rotate to switch between P, A, S, M, Auto, and custom modes.
Half-press to focus and meter exposure. Full press captures the image.
Adjust from -5 to +5 EV in 1/3 stop increments.
Direct ISO control from 64 to 102400, plus Auto ISO.

subsection.paragraph: The rear panel provides access to playback, menu navigation, and secondary shooting controls.
subsection.control: Opens the camera's settings menu hierarchy.
Activates autofocus independently of the shutter button (Back-button AF).
Navigate menus and images using the directional pad.

section.section-title: Inserting the Battery and Memory Card
section.step: Ensure the camera is powered off before opening the battery and card compartment door.
Slide the compartment door lock to the OPEN position and open the door.
Insert the battery with the contacts facing inward. Push until the battery latch clicks into place.
Insert the CFexpress or SD memory card in the appropriate slot. The card is correctly inserted when it clicks.
Close the compartment door and slide the lock to the CLOSED position.
section.caution: Never force the battery or memory card into the slot. Incorrect insertion may damage contacts.

section.paragraph: In Program Auto mode, the camera automatically selects the optimal shutter speed and aperture combination based on the metered exposure. You retain control over ISO, white balance, and other parameters.
section.tip: Use Program Shift to rotate the command dial and select alternative equivalent exposure combinations while maintaining correct exposure.

section.paragraph: You set the aperture and the camera automatically calculates the correct shutter speed. This mode is ideal for controlling depth of field.

A wide aperture (low f-number like f/1.8) produces a shallow depth of field with blurred backgrounds, ideal for portraits. A narrow aperture (high f-number like f/16) keeps more of the scene in sharp focus, ideal for landscapes.

You set the shutter speed and the camera calculates the correct aperture. Use fast shutter speeds (1/1000s or faster) to freeze motion and slow shutter speeds (1/30s or slower) for motion blur and light trails.
section.warning: At very slow shutter speeds without a tripod, camera shake will cause blurred images.

section.paragraph: Full manual control over both aperture and shutter speed. The exposure meter in the viewfinder shows whether your current settings will result in correct, over, or underexposed images.
Manual mode is preferred by professionals for studio photography, video production, and any situation where consistent exposure across multiple frames is required.

problem.cause: Battery is depleted or not inserted correctly
problem.solution: Charge the battery using the included charger. Ensure the battery is seated correctly with the latch clicked into place.

problem.cause: Camera shake at slow shutter speeds, or subject is out of focus
problem.solution: Use a faster shutter speed, enable image stabilization, or use a tripod. Verify the correct AF point is selected on your subject.

problem.cause: Card is not inserted correctly, is damaged, or is an unsupported format
problem.solution: Remove and reinsert the card. Format the card in-camera if it was previously used in another device. Use a CFexpress Type B or UHS-II SD card.
